correctness.rationale: The exact Khovanova–Lewis coefficient f_n(a,b)=[n−1 choose a+b−2]binom(a+b−2,a−1) implies the normalized bivariate PGF ∏_{j=0}^{n−2}(j+z+w)/(j+2). Each factor gives an independent increment in {(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)} with probabilities j/(j+2),1/(j+2),1/(j+2). The means of both record counts are H_n; variances H_n−H_n^(2)~log n, covariance 1−H_n^(2)=O(1). On Fourier scales θ=u/sqrt(log n), φ=v/sqrt(log n), cumulant sums give a standard independent two-coordinate Gaussian limit. Uniform domination is obtained from |j+e^{iθ}+e^{iφ}|²=(j+2)²−2j(2−cosθ−cosφ)−2(1−cos(θ−φ)), so |φ_n|≤exp[−c log n(θ²+φ²)] on [−pi,pi]². Rescaled Fourier kernels converge in L1 by dominated convergence; inversion then gives a uniform absolute error over all integer phases, stronger than weak convergence. The closest-integer point establishes the modal asymptotic and any distant maximizer contradicts the Gaussian bound. An independent count of every permutation through n=8 matches all Stirling-binomial cells. The theorem does not give relative tail errors or exact finite-n modes.

value.rationale: The maximum coefficient sequence is a natural, published skyscraper-permutation integer invariant (OEIS A218531). An explicit sharp leading constant 1/(2pi), factorial/logarithmic growth and localization of every maximizer answer a meaningful asymptotic enumeration question not determined by a finite table or a weak CLT alone. It does not claim a new generic local-limit method.

final_claim: For left- and right-to-left record maxima X_n,Y_n of a uniformly random permutation, their joint lattice mass admits a uniform additive bivariate Gaussian local limit on scale log n centered at H_n; consequently the largest count of permutations with specified left/right visibility is n!/(2 pi log n)(1+o(1)), and every maximizing pair has both coordinates log n+o(sqrt(log n)).
limitations: Uniform additive normalized bivariate lattice LCLT, not a relative far-tail estimate.
Does not determine a unique exact maximizing pair for finite n.
